packages.label: פְּגַם הַבְּרִית
packages.reason: All seven nodes in this cluster share the same essential nature: they are different faces of the single spiritual reality of defilement produced by covenant-transgression. The hub concept מי שפגם בבריתו (the covenant-violator) is directly equated via bechina edges to: מיין מרירין (bitter waters), מרה (bitterness), חרב פיות (the double-edged sword), and גיהנם (Gehinnom). Radiating outward from מיין מרירין are two further bechina-equivalents: מיין מסאבין (defiled waters) and זרע טמא (impure seed). Every node in this component is an aspect of the same reality — the spiritual pollution of the person who has violated the covenant. The Rebbe's proof-text structure makes this explicit: the covenant-violator IS bitter waters (line 6), and bitter waters IS the dog (line 7), IS Mara (line 7), IS the double-edged sword (line 7), IS Gehinnom (line 7). The dominant node is מי שפגם בבריתו with 4 direct bechina connections.

packages.label: שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית
packages.reason: This package groups all nodes in Torah #50 belonging to the positive/holy domain. Component B (4 nodes) forms the core: מיין מתיקין (sweet waters) = מיין דדכין (pure/clean waters) = זרע קדש (holy seed) = תקון הברית (guarding the covenant). These four are parallel names for the same spiritual reality — the purity that flows from guarding the covenant. The bechina equations are explicit in line 3 of the source text: 'מַיִּין מְתִיקִין זֶה בְּחִינַת מַיִּין דְּדַכְיָן, זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ, שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית.' The dominant nodes are מיין דדכין and זרע קדש, each with 2 bechina connections, sharing the hub role. Component C (2 nodes: עצם, אריה) is merged into this package by shared essential nature: the Rebbe teaches that when a person has pure waters (the covenant-keeper's essence), his words enter his bones and the bones feel their sweetness — bone IS a bechina of lion (line 5: 'עֶצֶם זֶה בְּחִינַת אַרְיֵה'). The lion (not the dog) accepts the covenant-keeper's sacrifice as salvation. Bones and lion are not cause-and-effect extensions of the pure-waters cluster — they are parallel aspects of the same holy domain: the spiritual dimension of covenant-keeping as it manifests in speech, body, and divine reception. The merge is by shared essential nature, not by eitza flow.

merge_notes.reason: The bone-lion pair (Component C) was isolated from Component B in the raw graph — no direct bechina edge connects עצם or אריה to any node in Component B. The framework requires merging 2-node isolated components into the thematically nearest larger package by shared nature. The nature of עצם-אריה is unambiguously the positive/holy domain: line 5 of the source text states 'עֶצֶם זֶה בְּחִינַת אַרְיֵה' in the context of the covenant-keeper's prayer. When the covenant-keeper has pure/sweet waters, his words enter his bones and the lion (not the dog) accepts his sacrifice as salvation. The lion is explicitly the positive counterpart of the dog: where the dog (Package 1, evil) devours the prayer of the covenant-violator, the lion (holy) receives the sacrifice of the covenant-keeper. The bone-lion pair shares its essential spiritual nature with the pure-waters cluster — both are aspects of holiness and covenant-keeping. This is a merge by shared essential nature (bechina domain), not by causal flow (eitza).

excluded_edges.reason: Excluded: type=eitza, not bechina. This edge describes a causal flow (covenant-repair PRODUCES ability to taste sweetness in prayer), not a parallel-nature equation.

Component C (2 nodes) — עצם/אריה → merged into Package 2 by shared nature (good). No component merged across polarity lines.
stats.note_on_mirror: The good/evil mirror structure in Torah #50 is structurally perfect: Package 1 (bitter/defiled waters, evil seed, sword, Gehinnom, bitterness) is the exact evil mirror of Package 2 (sweet/pure waters, holy seed, guarding covenant, bones, lion). Every concept in Package 1 has a direct parallel in Package 2 — מיין מרירין mirrors מיין מתיקין, זרע טמא mirrors זרע קדש, and the dog (כלבא, not yet in dataset) mirrors the lion (אריה).
